takeaways: Out of the box, Copilot only sees content inside Microsoft 365, while much of an organization's knowledge lives in legacy wikis, CRMs and file shares.
Plugins add narrow, specific skills, custom data integrations need ongoing development, and Graph connectors broaden what Copilot can see at scale.
Graph connectors index external data while honoring existing permissions, so Copilot can answer business questions without risky data migrations.
hook: Copilot gives generic answers because it cannot see the wikis, old CRMs and ticketing systems where your real knowledge lives. This episode is for Microsoft 365 developers, admins and architects who want Copilot to understand their business. Learn when to use plugins or custom integrations and why Graph connectors are usually the best way to bring legacy data into Copilot securely.
